newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair defends govt contacts with Sinn Fein.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair defends govt contacts with Sinn Fein.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair on Wednesday defended recent government contacts with Sinn Fein, saying it must not be able to claim that proposals to allow it to enter talks on Northern Ireland's future have not been fully explained.

Blair was accused in parliament by Ulster Unionist MP Jeffrey Donaldson of having broken a promise given after the shooting dead of two policemen in the town of Lurgan that there would be no communication with the IRA's political wing.
He confirmed that the government had responded since then to Sinn Fein letters and telephone calls.

"I want a situation where either Sinn Fein give up violence and come into inclusive (all-party) talks or if they do not, it is absolutely clear that they are not coming into those talks because they will not give up violence," Blair told Donaldson.
"And if it has to be given clarification so that everyone is under no doubt as to the government's position, that will be done," he added during the exchange at Prime Minister's Question Time.
Blair repeated that no party would be allowed into the talks "unless they give up violence unequivocally and clearly".
